header.title: Open Calc Studio
header.heroAlt: Open Calc Studio: the estimate of a fictitious single-family house with chapters, items and calculation lines, the total at the top right and the properties of the selected row
header.label: Cost estimating
header.tagline: Build a complete construction estimate, without licence fees or closed formats
header.desc: Build your estimate from chapters, items and calculation lines with production norms and hourly rates; markups and VAT are calculated along. Read files from your old estimating program and deliver a report or the format your client asks for.

meta.description: Free, open-source construction cost estimating: chapters, production norms, rates and markups, reports, and exchange with STABU, RAW, IBIS-TRAD, WPCalc, CUF, FIEBDC-3 (.bc3), ÖNORM and IFC. For Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser.
meta.title: Open Calc Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

prompt.alt: Prompt & Estimate: on the left the request to add a concrete line with the financial proposal before and after, on the right the estimate
prompt.title: Type what you want, see what it costs first
prompt.desc: Ask in plain language to add a line or look up a total. You first get a proposal with the direct costs, the total and the VAT before and after, and per changed row what changes. Apply it in one go or reject it.

wizard.alt: Guided estimate, Costs step: per line the unit price, the labour and the production norm, with the total at the bottom
wizard.title: Step by step to a sound estimate
wizard.desc: Five steps take you through project, quantities, costs, markups and VAT, and a final check. Every change appears straight away in the full estimate, and the total at the bottom keeps up.

exchange.alt: The Import menu with IFC, CUF-XML, Excel, STABU, IBIS-TRAD, RAW, FIEBDC-3, ÖNORM, GAEB and XPWE, among others
exchange.title: Bring your work from your old estimating program
exchange.desc: Read estimates from WPCalc, BasCalc, IBIS-TRAD, CUF-XML, STABU and RAW, or from Excel with your own columns. Spanish .bc3, Austrian ÖNORM and German GAEB bills of quantities go in too. Deliver again as WPCalc, CUF, .bc3, ÖNORM or IFC.

report.alt: Main contract report of the fictitious single-family house with project details, chapters, subtotals and the contract sum
report.title: A clean estimate for your client
report.desc: Seven reports, from work description and main contract to tender sheet and post-calculation. Choose the report language separately from the app language: headings, units, numbers and dates follow it. Print, or create a PDF in the desktop app.

notice.text: Open Calc Studio is in public testing. We are looking for testers who work with .bc3 files or on a Mac, and native speakers for the translations.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From first estimate to tender sheet, in one app
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

structure.title: Chapters, items and calculation lines
structure.desc: A clear structure with automatic numbering. Drag rows, also to another chapter.

norms.title: Norms and hourly rates
norms.desc: A production norm per line and rate groups with their own hourly rates. Change an hours total and the norms scale along.

markups.title: Markups
markups.desc: General costs, overhead, guarantees, risk, profit, insurance and rounding, in the usual order.

vat.title: Standard and reduced VAT
vat.desc: Choose the rate per chapter, item or line; the totals use the right rate.

variants.title: Variants and versions
variants.desc: Put options side by side, keep snapshots and see which rows have changed.

sheets.title: Spreadsheets
sheets.desc: Sub-calculations with formulas inside the estimate itself, in a tab beside it.

prompt.title: Prompt & Estimate
prompt.desc: Questions and commands in plain language, with a financial proposal you review first. Free-form commands need an OpenAEC account or your own API key.

wizard.title: Guided estimate
wizard.desc: Five steps from project details to checks, on the same estimate as the full editor.

review.title: Review center
review.desc: Checks prices, sources and units of the active variant, and jumps to the row with the issue.

mcp.title: MCP for AI assistants
mcp.desc: An assistant such as Claude creates estimates, adds items, sets markups and produces a PDF.

dutch.title: WPCalc, BasCalc, IBIS-TRAD and CUF
dutch.desc: Read estimates from well-known Dutch estimating programs; write WPCalc and CUF back too.

stabu.title: STABU and RAW
stabu.desc: A STABU specification (.s01, .sufx) or RAW specification (.rsx, .rsu) as the basis for your estimate, and a RAW tender sheet as Excel.

bc3.title: FIEBDC-3 (.bc3)
bc3.desc: The Spanish exchange format in and out, tested on 22 real files: all amounts equal after the round trip.

onorm.title: ÖNORM A 2063
onorm.desc: Read Austrian bills of quantities (.onlv) and standard texts (.onlb), and export .onlv following the official schemas.

gaeb.title: GAEB and XPWE
gaeb.desc: Read German GAEB bills of quantities (.x83) and Italian and Czech estimates (XPWE, XC4).

excel.title: Excel, CSV and price lists
excel.desc: Map the columns of an Excel or CSV file yourself, and load price lists (ZSX, BMEcat) into your library.

ifc.title: IFC cost schedule
ifc.desc: Read and write an estimate as IfcCostSchedule, for exchange with BIM software.

reports.title: Seven reports
reports.desc: Work description, main contract, subcontracting, tender sheet, post-calculation and two extended overviews.

reportlang.title: Report in your client's language
reportlang.desc: Headings, units and the notation of numbers and dates follow the chosen report language.

pdf.title: Print and PDF
pdf.desc: With cover page, summary, page numbering and portrait or landscape. The PDF preview is in the desktop app.

ifclite.title: Quantities from a 3D model
ifclite.desc: Open an IFC file, click elements and take their quantities into the selected item.

pdfmeasure.title: Measure on a PDF drawing
pdfmeasure.desc: Set the scale with two points, measure lengths and areas, and keep the measurements with the estimate.

provenance.title: Origin of every quantity
provenance.desc: See whether a quantity comes from a PDF, IFC model or spreadsheet, with page or object and a warning when the source is missing.

workspaces.title: Workspaces and second screen
workspaces.desc: Save your layout for measuring, estimating or checking, and put the drawing on a second screen.

languages.title: 39 languages and five themes
languages.desc: Including right-to-left for Arabic, Persian, Hebrew and Urdu, and light, dark, Blueprint and high contrast.

download.title: Download v0.13.0
download.lead: Free, no account needed. For Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.browserNote: Rather not install anything? The app also runs in the browser.
download.label: Download
download.mobileNote: Open Calc Studio is made for a large screen. Open it on your computer, or try it here in the browser.

onlv.title: Read Austrian bills of quantities
onlv.desc: An .onlv becomes an estimate: groups become chapters, positions become items with number, quantity, unit, labour and material.

onlb.title: Standard texts as a catalogue
onlb.desc: An .onlb, such as LB-Hochbau with almost 20,000 positions, loads in about 0.3 seconds.

onlvexport.title: Export as .onlv
onlvexport.desc: Valid against the official Austrian Standards schemas; import, export and re-import show no difference.

bc3.title: .bc3 equal field by field
bc3.desc: Of 22 real files, 21 come back identical field by field; every price difference is explained in the report.

toplevel.title: Unit price at the top level too
toplevel.desc: An item without a chapter now gets a derived unit price, just like other items.

whatsnew.label: New in v0.13.0
whatsnew.title: After Spain, now Austria
whatsnew.desc: Open Calc Studio now reads and writes the Austrian exchange format ÖNORM A 2063, and the round trip with Spanish .bc3 files has been tightened further and backed up with a report and screenshots.

files.a: Your own .ifcCalc files, estimates from WPCalc, BasCalc, IBIS-TRAD and CUF-XML, STABU specifications (.s01, .sufx), RAW specifications (.rsx, .rsu), Spanish .bc3, Austrian ÖNORM (.onlv, .onlb), German GAEB (.x83), Italian and Czech XPWE and XC4, IFC with a cost schedule, and Excel or CSV. Price lists come in as ZSX or BMEcat.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. The web version works straight in the browser and your files stay on your own computer. For the PDF preview of reports there is the desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux.

price.q: What does Open Calc Studio cost?
price.a: Nothing. The app is free and open source under the LGPL-3.0 licence, with no subscription. Only free-form commands to the AI assistant use credit from your OpenAEC account or your own API key.

save.q: In which format is my work saved?
save.a: In an .ifcCalc file: open, readable JSON with a documented structure. Older files always open; the desktop app saves quietly every two minutes.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows (.exe or .msi), macOS on Apple Silicon (.dmg) and Linux (AppImage, .deb, .rpm and Snap), and any modern browser. The Mac version is not yet notarized by Apple: the first time, you allow it once under Privacy & Security.

practice.a: Yes. The structure with norms, rate groups, markups and standard and reduced VAT follows Dutch practice, and STABU, RAW and the tender sheet go in or out. For Spain, Austria and Germany there are .bc3, ÖNORM and GAEB.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: In the app, Prompt & Estimate helps with questions and proposals you review first. There is also an MCP server (Model Context Protocol): with it, an assistant such as Claude creates estimates, adds items, sets markups and produces a PDF.

desktop.q: Are the newest features already in the desktop app?
desktop.a: Not yet. Prompt & Estimate, the guided estimate, the review center, measuring on PDF and quantities from a 3D model are in the web version now. They come to the installers with the next release; v0.13.0 does not have them yet.

export.q: Which formats can I export to?
export.a: PDF, CSV, IFC, WPCalc, CUF-XML, .bc3, ÖNORM (.onlv) and the RAW tender sheet as Excel. Export to IBIS-TRAD and RAW-RSX is limited; there is no GAEB export yet.

status.q: Is it ready for real work?
status.a: It is in public testing: stable enough to work with, but check your results and expect changes. Report what you find on GitHub; testers with .bc3 files or a Mac are especially welcome.

tauri.desc: A native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, with calculations and PDF layout in Rust.

react.desc: The same interface in the browser and on the desktop, with a virtualized grid for large estimates.

typst.desc: Modern typesetting for the PDF reports, with clean tables and page numbering.

format.title: Open .ifcCalc format
format.desc: Readable JSON with its own versioning policy and automatic migration of older files.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.desc: Creates and edits estimate files from a conversation with an AI assistant, all the way to the PDF.

embed.title: Embedding
embed.desc: A React/JavaScript SDK, iframe embedding and a native library (DLL, .so, .dylib) in the source code, for your own software.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.
